text.p: Interneuron Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Friday its Redux anti-obesity drug has hit the two-million-prescription mark six months after the drug's U.S. launch.
"We've now probably reached the two-million-prescription mark, which represents an excellent uptake into the marketplace for the agent," Interneuron chief executive Glenn Cooper said in an interview.
The FDA approved the Genentech drug for use only in patients who can be treated within three hours of an attack.
"Twenty-four hours is enough to capture the vast majority of stroke patients," Cooper said.

Interneuron acquired the U.S. rights to citicoline from Spanish pharmaceutical company Grupo Ferrer. Interneuron is talking with major pharmaceutical companies about possible partnership deals for marketing citicoline, Cooper said.
The company's majority-owned subsidiary Intercardia Inc , has a drug for treating congestive heart failure, bucindolol, in late-stage Phase III trial.
Results of a trial to determine the optimal dose of the drug should be out by the end of 1997, which, if positive, could lead to a larger confirmatory trial, Cooper said.

Interneuron's stock, however, has declined in the second half of the year, which Cooper attributed to a general softness in biotech stocks. On Friday Interneuron was down 1/2 at 21, off of its 52-week high of 44-1/2.
"Our valulation now is lower than when (Redux) was launched," he said. "In my view there hasn't been any significant negatives in the company's fundamentals during the period the stock has declined."
